A novel by John Dank · Book One

THE GARDEN

“The lights didn’t just go out in Atlanta; the future did.”

For Marcus, the collapse of the grid isn’t a tactical problem — it’s a heartbreak. As the “Godzilla” of greed and entropy stomps through the ruins of civilization, Marcus is forced to lead his ten-year-old son into a silence that feels heavier than any storm.

Walk the journey Skip to the book

Meet the survivors

Click a face. These are the people of The Garden — in the author’s own words.

The Godzilla

Every apocalypse has a monster. In The Garden it isn’t a creature — it’s a Godzilla made of greed and entropy, stomping through every system people trusted to hold.

The survivors can’t shoot it. They can only decide what they’ll feed it — and what they’ll refuse to.

The Journey

Seventeen chapters. Seventeen cliffhangers. Every image below is the book’s own chapter art — and every stop ends exactly where the chapter leaves you: needing the next page.

The False Calm
